h1.name: Hyundai H-1 2.5 CRDi
where: DIESEL ONLY. Never petrol. If someone puts petrol in, don’t start the engine: call the vehicle coordinator.
Turn the key to ON and wait until the yellow coil-shaped glow plug light goes out, then start.
Pull the release lever low down inside the cab (it shows a car with its bonnet open), then push the safety catch under the front edge of the bonnet and lift.
In the storage compartment under the front passenger seat. Open the cover to reach them.

Under the back of the van, held up by a lowering mechanism. The owner’s manual (“Removing and storing the spare tire”) shows where the jack handle fits to lower it. Practise once at the base, not on the roadside.
Under the bonnet, at the front of the engine bay.
On the sticker on the driver’s door frame. Use the full-load pressure when the van carries a full team and luggage.
On both sides. The child locks are on the edge of each sliding door.
weak: Turbo wear (from about 80 000 km)
Loss of power, black or blue smoke, a whistle or squeal when accelerating, and the engine using more oil.
Automatic gearbox
Jerky or late gear changes, especially from 1st to 2nd, or when you press the accelerator hard.
Steering and suspension wear
Uneven tyre wear, a shaking steering wheel, or vague steering. Vans that carry heavy loads wear faster.
Cold-morning starting
Needs several tries on cold mornings: glow plugs, the fuel filter or a weak battery.
Water pump and cooling
Coolant level dropping, a sweet smell, or the temperature needle climbing.
Aircon compressor
The aircon stops blowing cold, common in hot climates.
Rear brakes
Wear faster with heavy loads: listen for squealing or grinding.

item.drv-start: Wait for the coil-shaped glow plug light to go out before turning the key to start.
item.eng-batt: On the H-1 the battery is at the front of the engine bay.
item.saf-jack: On the H-1 the jack and spanner live under the front passenger seat.
item.tyr-spare: On the H-1 the spare is under the back of the van. Check it’s held up tight and the lowering mechanism isn’t rusted.
item.ext-slide: The H-1 has a sliding door on each side: check both.

t5.name: VW T5 Kombi 2.0 TDI
where: DIESEL ONLY. Never petrol. If someone puts petrol in, don’t start the engine: call the vehicle coordinator.
Turn the key to ON and wait until the yellow coil-shaped glow plug light goes out, then start.
Pull the release lever low down inside the cab (it shows a car with its bonnet open), then release the catch under the front edge of the bonnet and lift.
Under the driver’s seat, not under the bonnet.
In a carrier under the back of the van, held up by bolts that you undo with the wheel spanner. It’s awkward: practise once at the base.
On the sticker inside the fuel flap or on the driver’s door frame.
Kept at the workshop that services it.
weak: DSG gearbox
Jerky or hesitant pulling away, changes that don’t happen or pick the wrong gear, or erratic shifting.
EGR cooler (cooling system)
Coolant level drops with no puddle under the van, white steam from the exhaust, or the temperature needle climbing.
Sliding door
Won’t open from outside, hard to open or close, doesn’t close fully, or the dashboard says a door is open when it isn’t.
Engine noises
Metallic noises, rough idling or hard starting: get it checked straight away.
Turbo and boost
Loss of power and black smoke under load.

item.eng-batt: On the Kombi the battery is under the driver’s seat.
item.tyr-spare: On the Kombi the spare hangs in a carrier under the back. Check the bolts aren’t rusted solid.
item.ext-slide: The Kombi’s sliding door is on the left side.
item.drv-gears: DSG gearbox: pulling away should be smooth, with no jerk or hesitation.
item.eng-cool: On the Kombi, a coolant level that keeps dropping with no visible leak can be the EGR cooler: tell the workshop.
item.drv-start: Wait for the coil-shaped glow plug light to go out before starting.

crv.name: Honda CR-V 2.0
where: Pull the release lever low down by the driver’s door, then push the catch under the front edge of the bonnet and lift.
Under the boot floor: lift the floor panel.
On the sticker on the driver’s door frame.
Known not to close properly: always check it’s locked.
weak: Aircon blowing warm
The most reported problem on this generation of CR-V: cool at first, then warm, or not cold at all.
Door lock motors
A door, often the driver’s, doesn’t lock or unlock with the remote, or the lock buzzes.
Rear brakes
A grinding noise from the back brakes, from rust on the brake parts.
Battery
Goes flat if the car stands for a while: watch for slow starting.

item.ext-tail: This CR-V’s tailgate doesn’t close properly: pull on it to check it’s locked.
item.tyr-spare: On the CR-V the spare is under the boot floor.

almera.name: Nissan Almera 1.5
where: Unleaded PETROL only. Never diesel. The tank holds about 41 litres.
Pull the release lever low down by the driver’s door, then push the catch under the front edge of the bonnet and lift.
A full-size spare under the boot floor: lift the floor panel.
On the sticker on the driver’s door frame.
weak: Automatic gearbox
A few gearbox failures have been reported in South Africa: watch for slipping, harsh or late gear changes.
Boot-lid handle
Known to need repair on this car: check the boot opens with the handle.

item.tyr-spare: The Almera has a full-size spare under the boot floor.
